the histopathological reaction patterns in neutrophilic skin diseases, in particular with the neutrophilic epiteliotropic pattern, which has been described for the first time in this study.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
neutrophilic dermal infiltrate focally involving the epithelia of the adnexal structures is a characteristic histopathological finding in NUD.
neutrophilic dermal infiltrates in urticarial dermatitis are not sufficient for the diagnosis of NUD and that neutrophil epitheliotropisms is a histopathological clue to NUD.
NUD is a neutrophil-rich urticarial eruption with neutrophilic perivascular and epidermal infiltrates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

neutrophilic inflammation in the skin is not a simple process, but a complex one that is characterized by the involvement of the epidermis, dermis and adnexa, in particular hair follicles, sweat and sebaceous glands.
neutrophilic dermato-histopathology is a new and useful tool for the differential diagnosis of NUD.
the neutrophils in NUD are not confined to the dermis but also invade into the epithelia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
neutrophilic inflammation of the epidermis, in particular the epithelium, can be used as a diagnostic clue for NUD.
the presence of neutrophil epitheliotropia in a skin biopsy of a patient presenting with urticarial lesions and systemic symptoms should be interpreted as a sign of NUD.
neutrophilic epiteliotropism can be considered a new histopathological reaction type within the group of neutrophil-rich skin lesions.
